 Turnstile to perform Washington Monument benefit show 
 "All donations will go to Human Concern International, divided equally among its humanitarian efforts in Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon," the band said. 
 By Sachini Adikari • 
 Published October 23, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 23, 2026 at 6:28 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Will Heath/NBC 
 Musical guest Turnstile performs “Birds” on Saturday Night Live October 3, 2026 — (Photo by: Will Heath/NBC via Getty Images)
 The Baltimore rock band Turnstile will play a free concert at the Washington Monument Saturday afternoon.
 The benefit concert, while free, will raise donations. 
 Stream NBC4 newscasts for free right here, right now.
   WATCH HERE 
 "All donations will go to Human Concern International, divided equally among its humanitarian efforts in Palestine, Sudan, and Lebanon," they said. 
 The show begins at 3 p.m. The concert is open to all ages and will follow National Park Service guidelines for prohibited items .
 The concert is the last show in part two of the band’s “Never Enough” Tour. Part one began on May 10, 2025, with a free show in Baltimore that raised $35,000 for Health Care for the Homeless with over 10,000 people in attendance .

 Turnstile made their “Saturday Night Live” debut Oct. 3, performing “BIRDS” and “I CARE/DULL” live at Studio 8H.
 At the Grammy Awards earlier this year, the band won two Grammys for best rock album for "Never Enough" and best metal performance for "BIRDS."
 The band consists of singer Brendan Yates, drummer Daniel Fang, bassist Franz Lyons and guitarists Meg Mills and Pat McCrory.
 Yates, who is originally from Burtonsville, Maryland, attended Paint Branch High School in the late 2000s. Fang, the band’s drummer, grew up in Prince George’s County.
 Yates started the band in 2010 with ex-guitarist Brady Ebert, who was charged with attempted murder for allegedly intentionally hitting the singer’s father with a car . Turnstile released a statement in April, saying the band had cut ties with Ebert in 2022 in response to a “consistent pattern of harmful behavior affecting himself, the band, and the community.”
 A former guitarist for Grammy-winning Baltimore band Turnstile allegedly hit the singer's dad with a car. News4's Jackie Bensen reports.
